facts.assertion: Lambeth's 24 March 2026 New Homes Programme update says the borough aims to enable at least 10,000 new homes over the next decade.
The same March 2026 update states an aim for 40 per cent social and affordable housing across the development pipeline.
Fenwick Place is described as a completed 27-home development providing 100% council-rent homes.
Somerleyton Road Phase 2 had planning permission for 378 new homes in the March 2026 update.
The Somerleyton Road Phase 2 programme states 56% affordable housing.
The March 2026 update expected Somerleyton Road Phase 2 construction to start in 2026-2027.
The 49 Brixton Station Road redevelopment planning submission was expected to deliver 288 new homes.
The 49 Brixton Station Road proposal included almost 100 social-rent and affordable homes.
Lambeth's New Homes Hexagon partnership with Countryside was described as delivering around 500 homes across six council-owned sites.
The March 2026 update describes Leigham Court Road as a 92-home development.
The March 2026 Leigham Court Road update says half of the homes are social-rent and affordable homes.
The March 2026 update expected Leigham Court Road construction to start in 2026-2027.
Lambeth's 19 November 2025 announcement says planning approval had been secured for the Leigham Court Road scheme.
The November 2025 announcement says half of the Leigham Court Road homes would be affordable.
The November 2025 announcement specifies 15 social-rent homes for Lambeth residents on the housing register.
Lambeth owned the Leigham Court Road car-park site and entered an agreement with Pocket Living to combine it with a neighbouring site.

The November 2025 announcement estimated construction would begin in early 2026, while the later March 2026 update moved the expected start window to 2026-2027; the later source is treated as the current programme statement.
A March 2025 agreement for Leigham Court Road referred to a minimum of 14 new social-rent homes before the later planning approval referred to 15 social-rent homes.
Lambeth states that final planning-application decisions can be made under delegated powers or by the Planning Applications Committee.
Lambeth notes that most planning permissions are granted subject to conditions, so permission alone does not prove completed delivery or candidate parcel binding.
